elements.element: Customer owns every Deliverable created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 expressly states that Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer.

elements.element: Customer owns all other work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause addresses defined Deliverables only and does not cover work product that may fall outside that term.

elements.element: Vendor assigns every Deliverable created for Customer to Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 expressly states that Vendor assigns every Deliverable created for Customer to Customer.

elements.element: Vendor assigns all other work product created for Customer to Customer.
elements.evidence: No assignment of work product outside the Deliverable category is included.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing IP.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3 states that Vendor retains Vendor Technology, but the supplied language does not define Vendor Technology or establish that it includes all of Vendor's pre-existing IP.

elements.element: Customer receives a licence to any Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 expressly licenses any Vendor IP embedded in a Deliverable.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor IP is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 expressly describes the licence as perpetual.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 expressly describes the licence as irrevocable.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 expressly describes the licence as royalty-free.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: Section 14.1 states that Customer owns all Customer Data and gives Vendor only a limited processing right.

elements.element: No joint ownership is created.
elements.evidence: Section 14.4 states that no jointly owned IP is created absent a separate signed instrument. No such instrument is supplied, so the exception is not shown to be triggered.

elements.element: Vendor owns generic tools.
elements.evidence: The clause does not expressly reserve ownership of generic tools to Vendor. Retention of undefined Vendor Technology is insufficient to demonstrate this requirement.

elements.element: Vendor owns know-how.
elements.evidence: The clause does not expressly reserve ownership of know-how to Vendor, and the scope of Vendor Technology is not provided.

elements.element: Customer receives a licence to use Deliverables.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 expressly grants Customer a licence to use a Deliverable.

elements.element: Customer receives a licence to modify Deliverables.
elements.evidence: The express licence is limited to use and does not grant a modification right. Customer's ownership does not cure the omission for embedded Vendor IP, which is also licensed only for use.

elements.element: Customer receives a licence to sublicense Deliverables.
elements.evidence: No sublicensing right is granted, including with respect to embedded Vendor IP.

elements.element: The licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 expressly describes the use licence as perpetual.

elements.element: The licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 expressly describes the use licence as irrevocable.

elements.element: The licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: No worldwide or other affirmative territorial scope is stated.

elements.element: The licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 expressly describes the use licence as royalty-free.

elements.element: Customer may exercise the licensed rights for its business.
elements.evidence: The use licence contains no field-of-use restriction and therefore permits use for Customer's business, although modification and sublicensing rights remain absent.

result.reason: The preferred position is incomplete because work product outside the Deliverable category is neither owned nor assigned, and the undefined Vendor Technology reservation does not demonstrably cover all pre-existing Vendor IP. The fallback is also incomplete because generic tools and know-how are not expressly reserved, and the licence omits modification, sublicensing, and worldwide scope. The redline otherwise preserves Customer Data ownership and the default prohibition on joint ownership, and Sections 14.2 and 14.3 can generally be read together as ownership of the Deliverable subject to retained embedded Vendor Technology. Drafting quality is reduced by the redundant licence to a Customer-owned Deliverable, the narrow use-only scope for embedded Vendor IP, and the unexplained Section 13.2 cross-reference.
